bib.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences

question: Can deep RL agents learn complex tasks from non-expert human preferences between short trajectory segments, with feedback on a tiny fraction of interactions?
hypothesis: A reward predictor fit to pairwise comparisons, trained asynchronously with the policy, can match RL on the true reward using orders of magnitude less human feedback.
contributions: Scale reward learning from human preferences to deep RL (Atari, MuJoCo)
Feedback on less than 1% of agent interactions
Learn novel behaviours (backflip, one-legged cheetah, Enduro keep-alongside) with about an hour of human time
Ablations of ensembling, online queries, clip length, comparisons vs scores

method.summary: A policy (A2C for Atari, TRPO for MuJoCo) maximises a reward predictor fit with a Bradley-Terry cross-entropy loss to human (or synthetic oracle) comparisons of 1-2 s clips. Predictor, policy and labelling run asynchronously; queries are chosen by maximum ensemble disagreement.
method.task: RL with unobserved reward, learned from pairwise preferences over trajectory segments

datasets.name: MuJoCo tasks via OpenAI Gym (8 robotics tasks plus pendulum)
datasets.preprocessing: Episode termination replaced by a penalty; torque penalties removed

datasets.name: Atari (7 games: BeamRider, Breakout, Enduro, Pong, Qbert, SpaceInvaders, Seaquest)
datasets.preprocessing: Mnih 2015 wrappers; score area blacked out; life-loss/episode-end signals not sent to agent; rewards clipped to [-1,1]

datasets.name: Human preference labels
datasets.size: 700 queries (MuJoCo), 5,500 queries (Atari) in main runs; 900 (backflip), 800 (one-leg cheetah), ~1,300 (Enduro)
datasets.split: 1/e of data held out as validation per predictor
datasets.source: Contractors for main tasks; authors for Reacher, Cheetah and novel behaviours
datasets.preprocessing: Ties give uniform mu; 'can't tell' dropped

models.name: Reward predictor, MuJoCo
models.architecture: 2-layer MLP, 64 hidden units each, leaky ReLU alpha=0.01

models.name: Reward predictor, Atari
models.architecture: 84x84x4 input; 4 conv layers 7x7,5x5,3x3,3x3 strides 3,2,1,1, 16 filters each, leaky ReLU alpha=0.01, batch norm and dropout 0.5; FC 64; scalar output

other.lr: 0.0007 decayed linearly to zero after 80M timesteps (trained 50M)

training.objective: Cross-entropy between Bradley-Terry preference probability P(s1>s2)=exp(sum r1)/(exp(sum r1)+exp(sum r2)) and human label distribution mu; 10% uniform-random-response adjustment
training.optimizer: Atari policy: Adam (alpha=0.99, eps=1e-5); predictor optimizer not stated
training.lr: Atari policy 0.0007 linear decay; predictor lr not stated
training.lr_schedule: Atari policy linear to zero over 80M timesteps
training.warmup: Atari: reward predictor pretrained 200 epochs on 500 random-policy comparisons; MuJoCo: 25% of comparisons from random policy
training.weight_decay: l2 coefficient adapted to keep validation loss 1.1-1.5x train loss
training.dropout: 0.5 on Atari predictor conv layers; 'in some domains' otherwise
training.regularisation: l2 adaptive; ensemble of 3 predictors, each on |D| triples bootstrapped with replacement; 1/e held out
training.hardware: Atari: VM with 16 CPUs and one Nvidia K80 GPU
training.compute: about a day per Atari run, ~$25
training.seeds: 5 runs MuJoCo, 3 runs Atari for synthetic/RL curves; real human feedback a single run

other.label_rate_atari: decreased every 5e6 frames, roughly proportional to 5e6/(T+5e6)
other.candidate_pairs: 10x more clip pairs drawn than presented, picked by max variance across ensemble

metrics.name: True task reward
metrics.definition: Average reward under the underlying environment reward (not seen by agent), averaged over 5 batches (MuJoCo) or ~150,000 frames (Atari)

baselines: synthetic oracle feedback with 350, 700, 1400 (MuJoCo) or 350, 700, 1400, 3300 etc. labels (Atari)
ablations: random queries, no ensemble, no online queries, no regularization, no segments, target (regression on true segment reward)
eval.protocol: Mean of 5 (MuJoCo) or 3 (Atari) runs for synthetic and RL; real human feedback single run; no significance tests

evidence.quote: Training takes about a day, so the compute cost is ~$25.

results.claim: Feedback on a tiny fraction of interactions suffices
results.quote: providing feedback on less than 1% of our agent’s interactions with the environment

results.claim: Interaction complexity is cut by roughly 3 orders of magnitude by a separate reward model
results.setup: vs using human feedback directly as reward
results.quote:
it is possible to reduce the interaction
complexity by roughly 3 orders of magnitude

results.claim: With 700 labels MuJoCo agents nearly match RL on the true reward
results.setup: 8 MuJoCo tasks + pendulum, human or synthetic feedback, 5 runs for synthetic, human single run
results.quote: With 700 labels we are able to nearly match reinforcement learning on all of these tasks.

results.claim: By 1400 synthetic labels the agent slightly beats RL on the true reward, perhaps from better shaping
results.quote:
by 1400 labels our algorithm performs slightly better than if it had simply been given
the true reward

results.claim: Atari human feedback run used 5,500 queries; matches RL on some games, not others
results.quote: Figure 3 shows the results of training our agent with 5,500 queries to a human rater

results.claim: Hopper backflip trained with 900 queries in under an hour (feedback from authors)
results.setup: Hopper, same parameters as main runs, authors as labellers
results.quote:
This behavior was
trained using 900 queries in less than an hour.

results.claim: Half-Cheetah on one leg trained with 800 queries in under an hour (authors)
results.quote:
This behavior was
trained using 800 queries in under an hour.

results.claim: Enduro keep-alongside trained with about 1,300 queries and 4M frames (authors)
results.quote:
This was trained with roughly 1,300 queries

results.claim: Contractors answered the average query in 3-5 s; real-human experiments took 30 min to 5 h
results.setup: contractors, several hundred to several thousand pairs per task
results.quote: Contractors responded to the average query in 3-5 seconds

results.claim: Human feedback on Atari performs like synthetic feedback with 40% fewer labels
results.setup: Atari, comparable to synthetic with same label count
results.quote:
comparably to synthetic feedback that has 40%
fewer labels

results.claim: Offline (non-online) reward predictor training performs poorly and yields bizarre behaviour (Pong endless volleys)
results.setup: MuJoCo (700 synthetic labels, 5 runs) and Atari (5,500 synthetic labels, 3 runs)
results.quote:
human feedback needs to be intertwined with RL learning rather than
provided statically

results.claim: Cost: Atari compute about $25 vs about $36 of human labour for 5k labels
results.setup: K80 VM ~$700/month, one day training; 5k labels ~5 h at US minimum wage ~$36
results.quote: Training takes about a day, so the compute cost is ~$25.

results.claim: Ensemble disagreement query selection can impair performance on some tasks
results.quote: in some tasks it actually impairs performance

limits: Human feedback on novel behaviours came from the authors, not non-expert contractors
Real-human results are a single run per task; synthetic curves are 3-5 runs, no significance tests
Query selection by ensemble variance is described as crude and sometimes hurts
On Qbert real human feedback fails to beat the first level; human labels are uneven and inconsistent across contractors
Environment termination conditions were removed so as not to leak task information; no text/LM setting
Reward assumed a function of 4 preceding frames in Atari, ignoring general partial observability
Predictor optimizer, learning rate and batch size are not stated

terms.definition: a sequence of observations and actions of length k, here 1-2 seconds of video
labels are fed in at a rate decaying inversely with the number of timesteps
